tasks.short: Conduct exit interviews, complete termination paperwork, and coordinate approved departure records.

steps.what: Check the approved departure notice against the employee record and required departure checklist.
Arrange an exit interview with the departing employee.
Discuss departure reasons, listen to concerns, and take factual notes.
Write a restricted interview summary and separate concerns needing confidential follow-up.

loop.input: Factual interview notes and approved confidentiality and referral rules.
loop.output: A source-linked summary with proposed follow-up flags.
loop.check: The HR specialist checks attribution, omissions, sensitive details, and referral recipients before saving.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unclear or sensitive passages return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text accounts need careful condensation; templates cannot preserve their meaning alone.

steps.what: Prepare termination documents using approved dates, terms, and current templates.
Check termination paperwork and approve the departure instructions.
File approved documents and update the departure status.
Send approved payroll instructions and departure actions to responsible teams.

tasks.design: Configure departure checklists, document templates, filing, and approved notifications across the {HCM}, {DOCS}, {CALENDAR}, and {WORKFLOW}. A bounded drafting loop prepares restricted summaries from written notes for HR review; the exit conversation and termination approval stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departure records, document templates, and team handoffs often sit in separate places. Sensitive interview accounts also resist simple form filling.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow and template features handle most administration. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting them, while a bounded loop drafts summaries.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed departures, sensitive allegations, local document requirements, and access restrictions need careful handling. The employment decision must already be authorized.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, hear what an employee hesitates to say, and distinguish a routine departure from a concern requiring protection.

ambition.what: Monthly retention intervention triage using disclosure-controlled departure themes.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing forms toward confidential follow-up and testing retention interventions. No new authority over termination decisions follows automatically.

reach.task: Triage departure concerns for possible grievance handling.
reach.learn: Learn protected reporting routes, evidence preservation, and national consultation rules.

reach.task: Choose a targeted retention intervention from recurring departure themes.
reach.learn: Learn cohort analysis, small-group disclosure control, and intervention evaluation.

evidence.claim: Checklist automation, template merging, and approved notifications are established deterministic patterns; the proposed time shares are estimates.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment when a proposed process makes solely automated decisions with significant effects.
Dutch works council consent provisions cover specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; other countries require assessment under national rules.

assumptions: The process begins after an authorized departure decision; it does not decide dismissal terms.
The baseline represents a mid-size European employer with an HCM, document templates, and some email handoffs.
Written interviewer notes are sufficient; recording is not required.
Build ranges estimate working effort for one jurisdiction and an initial deployment; consultation may take longer in elapsed time.
Reusable templates provide a personal head start before employer-specific integrations are available.
unknowns: Which departure types, documents, and approval roles the employer uses.
Whether the HCM supports templates, workflow triggers, and approved document filing.
Who may see interview notes, follow-up referrals, and aggregate departure themes.
Which employee representatives must be consulted and what approvals already exist.
How often disputed departures or missing records occur.
research_questions: Which national termination, retention, and employee-consultation rules govern the intended deployment?
What disclosure controls make departure-theme reporting useful without exposing individuals?
new_work: Review generated summaries and route confidential concerns.
Handle incomplete records, disputed terms, and failed handoffs.
Maintain departure templates, approval routing, access permissions, and retention rules.
Check aggregate themes for small-group disclosure.

tasks.short: Interview applicants and record reliable evidence of work history, education, training, and skills.

steps.what: Arrange the interview and confirm any requested participation adjustments.
Read application documents and prepare job-related questions about missing or unclear evidence.

loop.input: Application documents, approved role criteria, and the interview guide.
loop.output: Source-linked factual evidence and proposed clarification questions, without a candidate score.
loop.check: Check source references, dates, unsupported inferences, and job relevance before using questions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unreadable or conflicting material goes to the interviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Work histories and skill descriptions use varied free text that fixed fields do not fully capture.

steps.what: Conduct the interview, probe examples, and explain the role and recruitment process.
Organize interview notes against the agreed evidence fields.

loop.input: Interviewer-written notes and approved evidence fields.
loop.output: A factual evidence draft separating candidate statements, observed examples, and unanswered questions.
loop.check: The interviewer checks each claim against notes; missing evidence remains explicitly missing.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; ambiguous passages remain for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Condensing narrative examples requires language interpretation beyond field copying.

steps.what: Ask the candidate to clarify material factual gaps.
Validate and save the interview evidence for the hiring manager.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling templates and structured evidence fields in the {ATS}, with approved communications through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. Bounded loops prepare source-linked questions and organize written notes; the interviewer conducts the conversation, checks the evidence, and approves the saved record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Candidate histories and interview notes are mostly narrative. Useful preparation needs interpretation, while interviewing itself depends on trust and responsive questioning.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce preparation and paperwork. Existing structured forms and scheduling features cover the deterministic work.
tasks.still_hard: Fair probing, participation adjustments, contradictory accounts, and recognizing transferable skills remain demanding. Model-generated wording can introduce unsupported impressions.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a fair follow-up, notice misunderstanding, and help candidates explain evidence without coaching them toward a preferred answer.

ambition.what: Career-returner skills interviews using explicit transferable-skill evidence.

tasks.altitude: The interviewer spends more time testing examples and less time rewriting notes. Selection authority remains with the existing decision-makers.

reach.task: Review interview questions and evidence fields for unequal barriers.
reach.learn: Learn accessible interviewing, job relevance, and how to audit patterns without inferring protected traits.

reach.task: Distinguish an essential entry skill from a trainable gap.
reach.learn: Learn competency mapping and evidence-based learning-needs assessment.

evidence.claim: Textkernel offers CV parsing and matching, supporting the feasibility of application extraction; it does not establish interview quality.
Recruitment and selection AI can fall within Annex III high-risk uses; classification depends on the intended function.
Workplace emotion recognition is a prohibited AI practice, subject to the stated legal exceptions; this design uses no emotion inference.
A determining automated score can engage GDPR automated-decision safeguards; adding a nominal reviewer is insufficient.
Conversation dominates this task, so preparation and recordkeeping improvements provide a limited overall time reduction.

assumptions: Interviews remain human-led and use approved job-related criteria.
The baseline uses email coordination, application review in an ATS, and written interview notes.
No audio recording, personality inference, automatic ranking, or rejection is needed.
Templates and interview guides can be reused personally; live candidate data requires authorized access.
Build ranges estimate working effort; national consultation and legal assessment can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which interview formats, evidence fields, and decision roles the employer uses.
Whether the ATS supports structured interview forms and authorized data exchange.
What participation adjustments and candidate notices are already supported.
Which languages and application formats occur in practice.
What employee consultation, privacy assessment, and access approvals already exist.
research_questions: How should the intended preparation tool be classified under current EU AI Act rules and applicable guidance?
Which national interviewing and accessibility requirements affect the approved guide?
What evaluation set can reveal unsupported claims and uneven extraction quality across application formats?
new_work: Review proposed questions and generated evidence drafts.
Resolve inconsistent dates, missing examples, and unclear candidate statements.
Maintain interview guides, participation instructions, and access controls.
Sample outputs for unsupported impressions and uneven treatment.

tasks.short: Find potential candidates, assess job-related evidence, and start appropriate recruitment conversations.

steps.what: Agree essential criteria, trainable skills, and suitable sourcing channels with the hiring manager.
Search existing candidate records using job-related criteria and permitted contact status.
Search job-board databases and review permitted candidate-source alerts.
Discuss referrals and opportunities with professional contacts, recruiting firms, and potential candidates.
Consolidate permitted profiles, remove duplicates, and capture source-linked experience evidence.

loop.input: Permitted profile documents, referral notes, approved evidence fields, and source references.
loop.output: Draft factual evidence fields with provenance and unresolved identity conflicts.
loop.check: Validate field types and source references; review uncertain identity matches and unsupported claims before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per profile; conflicts go to manual review without automatic merging.
loop.why_not_simpler: Deduplication is deterministic, but narrative experience needs bounded extraction into common fields.

steps.what: Decide which candidates merit an initial conversation using documented job-related evidence.
Write and send an appropriate initial approach to selected candidates.
Record outreach status, responses, and agreed next actions.

tasks.design: Configure saved searches in the {ATS} and permitted candidate-source databases in the {OTHER}, then consolidate results through the {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic checks handle permissions and duplicates, while bounded extraction prepares source-linked evidence for recruiter review. Recruiters choose outreach recipients and approve template-based messages through the {EMAIL}; responses update the {ATS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Candidate sources have different access terms, profile formats, and identifiers. Matching terminology and maintaining provenance require more than copying search results.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and standard connectors can cover much of retrieval and tracking. Bounded extraction handles narrative profiles without needing autonomous browsing or candidate ranking.
tasks.still_hard: Some sources restrict exports or lack usable interfaces. Candidate interest, transferable skills, weak referrals, and inclusive outreach still require human judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize plausible potential beyond familiar career paths and build enough trust for a candidate to consider a move.

ambition.what: Candidates from regional vocational retraining programmes.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated searching and copying toward testing new sourcing channels and speaking with candidates. Recruiters retain outreach choices; changes to essential criteria still need hiring-manager approval.

reach.role: compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialist
reach.task: Separate essential role requirements from habits inherited from previous vacancy descriptions.
reach.learn: Learn job analysis, skill equivalence, and how role requirements relate to job level.

reach.task: Assess whether sourcing channels systematically exclude qualified groups.
reach.learn: Learn lawful aggregate measurement, source coverage analysis, and bias-aware sampling.

evidence.claim: Textkernel provides CV parsing and matching, supporting factual profile extraction and search assistance.
AFAS Profit 8 offers application scoring per vacancy; this establishes capability, not suitability for automatic selection.
AI intended for recruitment and selection can fall within Annex III high-risk uses.
A score that determines a significant decision can engage GDPR automated-decision safeguards.
Saved searches, permission checks, template messages, and pipeline updates can largely use deterministic technology.

assumptions: The baseline combines ATS searches, candidate-source screens, referral conversations, and email outreach.
Existing ATS search filters and candidate-source alerts are adequate for the first version.
Only authorized sources and permitted exports are used; public visibility alone does not establish unrestricted reuse.
Existing connectors can capture communication metadata; interpreting complex replies remains human work.
A reusable sourcing brief and evidence template provide a head start without employer integrations.
Build ranges estimate effort for a limited initial source set; consultation and source licensing may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which candidate sources the employer can lawfully access, export, and connect.
Which ATS search, deduplication, and communication features are enabled.
What lawful bases, notices, retention periods, and contact restrictions apply to existing records.
How frequently the role uses fairs, advertisements, agencies, and referral networks.
Whether retraining partnerships exist and which roles could accept their candidates.
research_questions: What current source terms allow saved searches, exports, and profile reuse?
How should the intended extraction and search assistance be classified under current EU AI Act rules?
How can retrieval quality be tested for transferable skills without introducing automated exclusion?
new_work: Review uncertain profile extractions and duplicate identities.
Maintain source permissions, field mappings, search filters, and retention rules.
Approve outreach and handle objections or correction requests.
Sample missed candidates and compare channel coverage.
Monitor connector failures and source-format changes.

tasks.short: Help managers interview, appraise performance, counsel employees, and document concerns appropriately.

steps.what: Clarify the manager's learning need and identify any sensitive live employee situation.
Find current policies, interview guides, appraisal guidance, and documentation templates.
Prepare practical training materials, examples, and exercises for the manager group.

loop.input: Approved source pack, audience brief, and training templates; examples exclude identifiable live cases.
loop.output: A cited training draft with exercises, factual examples, and explicit limits.
loop.check: Check every policy statement against current sources and review examples for fairness and practical accuracy.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted correction passes; unsupported topics are omitted or referred to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but audience-specific explanations and practice scenarios require language generation.

steps.what: Enrol managers and issue joining instructions for the training session.
Teach the session, practise conversations, and challenge unsafe or unfair managerial assumptions.
Record attendance, completion, and agreed learning follow-up.
Answer follow-up questions and refer employee-specific matters for individual HR advice.

loop.input: A manager question and access-filtered, current approved guidance.
loop.output: A cited general guidance draft or a referral when the question needs individual advice.
loop.check: HR verifies source support and context before sending; employee-specific recommendations require personal handling.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one draft; missing, conflicting, or case-specific evidence triggers referral.
loop.why_not_simpler: Managers phrase questions unpredictably; fixed FAQs cannot cover every explanation or ambiguity.

tasks.design: Use a versioned source register in the {DOCS} to assemble approved guidance, then generate cited training drafts through a bounded loop. Configure enrolment and completion in the {LMS}; a reviewed answer desk drafts follow-up responses through the {EMAIL}. HR specialists lead practice sessions and take employee-specific advice out of the general guidance flow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies, examples, and manager questions vary, making training preparation repetitive but difficult to standardize completely. Source currency and live employee context limit unattended answers.
tasks.enabler_now: Document metadata and learning-system workflows cover administration. Bounded drafting can adapt approved content into exercises and explanations with traceable sources.
tasks.still_hard: Managers need practice and challenge, particularly around conflict and performance documentation. National employment rules, policy conflicts, and individual cases require specialist advice.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when a manager's framing is unfair, rehearse a difficult conversation, and explain the consequences of their choices.

ambition.what: A practice clinic before a manager's first performance conversation.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding training packs toward observed practice and targeted coaching. No new authority over employee performance or disciplinary decisions is created.

reach.task: Evaluate whether managers apply the training in practice.
reach.learn: Learn scenario assessment, learning transfer, and proportionate follow-up measurement.

reach.task: Review guidance for documenting performance concerns before a formal process.
reach.learn: Learn procedural fairness, escalation boundaries, and applicable national rules.

evidence.claim: Versioned source retrieval, template assembly, enrolment, and completion tracking are established deterministic patterns.
Source-bounded drafting can assist training preparation, but the digest provides no HR-training case proving the proposed gains.
The documented report failure involving invented sources supports checking generated citations before publication.
AI used for worker evaluation can fall within Annex III; a later expansion from training guidance into employee assessment needs separate classification.

assumptions: The baseline combines document preparation, an LMS, live teaching, and email follow-up.
Approved guidance has identifiable owners, versions, and effective dates.
Attendance can be captured through configured LMS functions; completion does not imply demonstrated competence.
Training examples use fictional or properly de-identified situations.
A personal starter pack can contain generic exercises; employer policy answers require approved local sources.
Build ranges estimate working effort for a small topic set; consultation applies where employee-data or monitoring changes require it.
unknowns: Which training topics, languages, and manager groups have the highest demand.
Whether policies have reliable version metadata and named content owners.
Which LMS scheduling, attendance, and completion functions are enabled.
Who may approve guidance and accept individual advice referrals.
Whether proposed learning measurements change employee monitoring or consultation obligations.
research_questions: Which national employment and consultation rules must the training sources reflect?
What scenario assessment would show better managerial practice without unnecessary employee monitoring?
How reliably can the proposed source checks detect outdated or conflicting guidance?
new_work: Review generated training packs and cited answers.
Maintain source versions, exercises, and referral boundaries.
Handle unanswered questions and individual employee situations.
Collect practice feedback and update weak training examples.
Check that completion records remain distinct from competence judgments.

role.altitude: The HR specialist spends less time transferring records and rebuilding documents, and more time interviewing, coaching, and resolving sensitive exceptions. Existing employment decision rights remain; broader authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Support labor relations triage with clear evidence and protected referral routes.
Work with equal opportunity representatives on interview fairness and sourcing coverage.
Help training and development specialists assess practical skill gaps and learning transfer.
Bring disclosure-controlled departure themes to HR managers for targeted retention decisions.
skills_to_grow: Map workflows, approval points, and data ownership.
Configure forms, templates, saved searches, and notifications.
Apply GDPR, relevant EU AI Act requirements, and national employment rules.
Handle confidential conversations and evidence-based interviewing.
Evaluate process quality, inclusion, and learning outcomes.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a reusable HR practice kit: structured interview guides, sourcing briefs, exit checklists, and manager exercises. Connect it to authorized employer systems, then offer career-returner interviews and manager practice clinics while people retain consequential decisions.
